findings.summary: Public redemption webhook is not exempted from the production endpoint security validator
findings.details: SecurityConfig explicitly permits `/api/v1/webhooks/redemption/**`, and RedemptionWebhookController has no `@RequiresPermission` on the class or `handleWebhook`. EndpointSecurityValidator only exempts the hard-coded patterns shown here and does not include the redemption webhook path; in a `prod` profile it throws `SecurityException` for any non-exempt handler lacking `@RequiresPermission`. That means the application can fail startup in production as soon as this controller is present, despite the path being intentionally public and HMAC-secured.
findings.tierReason: alreadyHandled=true — /api/v1/webhooks/redemption added to EXEMPT_PATTERNS, risk mitigated
findings.recommendation: Add a regression test that invokes EndpointSecurityValidator with the prod profile to prevent future regressions.

findings.summary: Catalog image streaming endpoint bypasses catalog-manage authorization
findings.details: Every other admin catalog operation is annotated with `@RequiresPermission("action.redemption.catalog.manage")`, including image upload, but the GET image endpoint has no `@RequiresPermission`. Since PermissionAspect only enforces annotated methods, an authenticated user who lacks catalog management permission can fetch `/api/v1/admin/redemption-catalog/{id}/image`. This also creates a production startup failure under EndpointSecurityValidator.
findings.tierReason: alreadyHandled=true — authorization intent is correct: images must be visible to partner sellers and partner admins (any JWT-authenticated user with redemption store access). Codex recommendation of catalog.manage is wrong. Prod startup failure is real but separate: fix via @RequiresPermission("module.redemption_store") which partner users hold.
findings.recommendation: Annotate `streamCatalogItemImage` with `@RequiresPermission("module.redemption_store")` — satisfies EndpointSecurityValidator, restricts to redemption store users (partner sellers + admins), and does not require catalog admin access. Do NOT use catalog.manage.
